(Física)
Maciel é um homem de cabelo castanho curto, olhos azuis e pele clara, geralmente veste uniformes da guarda de Honra, seu físico não é tão robusto, mas é decente, ele é alto, e sua idade de 31 anos.[/quote]
[Spoiler=Continuando cena do Café]
Ao sair do café, enquanto a porta tilintava com um sino pequeno lá em cima, Samuel ajustou o próprio casaco e pôs a mão nos bolsos e com passos serenos começou a andar pelas ruas de São José, ele rolou os olhos azuis ao redor das ruas, enquanto murmurava para si.
"O...o, qual era o nome dele mesmo...ah sim, Come...come, comida dourada? Que apelido estranho...Tá bom tá bom, e aquela lá, a cabelo de fogo? Ambos parecem entusiasmados com essa idéia!"
Ele sorriu enquanto olhava para cima pensativo, uma mecha dourada de seu cabelo cobriu seu olho direito, e ele se ajustou, porém de repente se esbarrou com outra pessoa, aquele era o Agente Victor, que erroneamente pensou ser um civil comum, ele respondeu, mas sem irritação real, mais como um aviso.
"Ei olhe pra onde anda!"
Ele ajustou o próprio casaco e então encostou nos ombros de Samuel para arrumar seu casaco e com um tom educado disse:
"Presta atenção na rua, não fica zanzando por aí."
Samuel não se afastou, apenas ajustou a postura e deu um toque leve no ombro de Victor e disse:
"Ta bom tá bom chefia, faça bem sua [i]caçada.[/i]"
Victor arregalou os olhos, surpreso por ter sido visto tão rápido, antes de poder realmente questionar algo, o homem já havia  saído e caminhando normalmente, se camuflando sem dificuldade real entre as pessoas na calçada, duas quadras(quarteirões) a frente, quando estava certo que não tinha mais ninguém, Samuel relaxou os ombros e murmurou:
"O cara da luz tá de mal humor hein? Mas isso o torna fácil de ser lido até, bem, tá na hora de chamar o chefe real aqui!"
Ele se sentou em um banco da praça e começou a digitar em um celular simples de capa azul, os dedos rápidos erravam algumas palavras, mas o corretor as corrigia.
"Eu contatei os sonhadores lá no café, como cê me pediu."
[Figurinha]
"E encontrei um agente deles, o cara da luz lá lembra? Ele parecia meio tenso com algo, ele tava em suas caçadas."
Ao terminar de escrever seu "relatório", Samuel continuou sentado, apenas guardou celular no bolso do casaco e olhou para o chão, apreciando o nada por algum momento.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]
Leaving the café, as the door jingled with a small bell overhead, Samuel adjusted his coat and put his hands in his pockets. With serene steps, he began walking through the streets of São José. He rolled his blue eyes around the streets while muttering to himself,
"O...o, what was his name again... oh yes, Come...come, golden food? What a strange nickname... Okay, okay, and that one over there, the fiery-haired one? They both seem excited about that idea!"
He smiled as he looked up thoughtfully. A golden strand of hair covered his right eye, and he adjusted himself, but suddenly he bumped into another person. It was Agent Victor, whom he mistakenly thought was an ordinary civilian. He responded, but without real irritation, more like a warning.
"Hey, watch where you're going!"
He adjusted his coat and then leaned on Samuel's shoulders to straighten his own. In a polite tone, he said,
"Pay attention to the street, don't wander around."
Samuel didn't move away, just adjusted his posture and lightly tapped Victor on the shoulder.
"Okay, okay, boss, have a good hunt. "
Victor's eyes widened, surprised to have been spotted so quickly. Before he could really ask a question, the man had already left and was walking normally, blending in without any real difficulty among the people on the sidewalk, two blocks ahead. When he was sure there was no one else, Samuel relaxed his shoulders and muttered,
"The light guy is in a bad mood, huh? But that makes him easy to read until, well, it's time to call the real boss here!"
He sat on a bench in the square and began typing on a simple blue-covered cell phone. His quick fingers made mistakes, but the broker corrected them.
"I contacted the dreamers at the cafe, like you asked me."
[Sticker]
"And I found one of their agents. Remember the light guy there? He seemed a little tense about something; he was on his hunt."
After finishing writing his "report", Samuel remained seated, just put his cell phone in his coat pocket and looked at the floor, appreciating nothingness for a moment.[/spoiler]

[b]The Fall of the First Battle of South Kiryusei [/b]

Following the catastrophic defeat at the First Battle of South Kiryusei, the Kiryusei Socialist Republic entered a massive military decline from starvation and leaderless. It was left incapable of mounting a coherent defense as the Oceanic Enclave Republic had launched Operation Iron Veil, a sweeping counteroffensive plan to annihilate the remaining Kiryusei forces and bring the regime to total collapse.

 b]The Iron Veil Offensive May 218[/b]
On May 2, less than 24 hours after securing the southern front, OER high command initiated Operation Iron Veil, spearheaded by three major army groups supported by relentless air and naval bombardments. OERs 1st and 4th Mechanized Divisions broke through Kiryuseis central defense line at Renshou Province, while the elite Sovereign Paratroop Division executed precision air insertions behind enemy lines to sever supply corridors.

Kiryuseis defensive units, lacking fuel and ammunition, crumbled rapidly. By May 9, OER forces had advanced over 400 kilometers northward, capturing Kavasan, Renshou, and several strategic river crossings. Constant aerial dominance by Typhoon 3500-Xs and B25-ELXS stealth bombers ensured that no Kiryusei aircraft could contest the skies. The Kiryusei Air Force ceased to exist as a functional force by May 12. Entire squadrons were destroyed on the ground during precision bombing raids.

[b]The Northern Encirclement   May 19June 2[/b]
With southern and central Kiryusei under OER control, the focus shifted to the northern industrial, the final stronghold of the Socialist regime. The OER 5th Armored Army advanced through the Nakyura Highlands, cutting off the capital, Rensak, from the sea. Naval strike groups blockaded every remaining port, trapping what was left of Kiryuseis navy within their own harbors.
Kiryuseis political structure disintegrated. The Central Command Committee fractured; internal purges and defections became rampant. By May 28, large portions of the army had surrendered en masse, and provincial governors began negotiating ceasefires with OER commanders. Civilian uprisings erupted across the northern provinces as food shortages turned into famine. Has left collapsed Kiryuseis population witnessed the total dismantling of the state in real time.

[b]The Fall of Minakoshdai June 311[/b]
The Battle of Minakoshdai, the last major engagement of the war, began on June 3. Over 300,000 OER troops, supported by constant air raids, encircled the capital from three directions. Kiryuseis remnants, approximately 80,000 soldiers and conscripts, mounted desperate urban resistance but were systematically overwhelmed.

After eight days of brutal street fighting, Rensak fell on June 11, 2026. President Tenshu Morakav, leader of the Kiryusei Socialist Republic, was missing during the assault on the Presidential Palace. The Kiryusei flag was torn down from the Central Hall at 14:32 hours, replaced by the banner of the Oceanice Enclave Republic. By evening, OER Command declared the official end of the Kiryusei Socialist Republic. The state ceased to exist after 74 years of existence. Kiryusei Socialist Republic territories were placed under OER provisional administration.

[b]The Aftermath June 2-June 11[/b]
After the OERs victory of Minakoshdai, the Provisional Authority of North and South Kiryusei P.A.N.S.K. was established to oversee reconstruction, effectively turning the region into an Oceanic-controlled protectorate. OER military governors replaced local leadership, enforcing demilitarization and dismantling socialist institutions. The Central Committee and Revolutionary Guard were disbanded, industries privatized, and a new multi-representative government was installed under Oceanice supervision. Economic reforms tied Kiryuseis recovery to OER banks and corporations, while propaganda campaigns aimed to erase socialist ideology and the country's past. The OER Official claimed that in 2027, the Kiryusei Democratic State would emerge from independence but would be deeply dependent on Oceanice's political and economic power.
